## Statement

An emulation makes many defensible decisions: active comparator, washout period, time zero, grace period, how treatment episodes are constructed, censoring rules, follow-up length and outcome definition. Each has more than one reasonable answer, and the set of answers is the researcher's degrees of freedom. Design guidance exists and states that the operational methods remain scenario dependent, so it narrows the set without closing it. Registrations record the specification that was finally run and not the alternatives considered, the order in which decisions were made, or which were revised after the data were inspected. A final protocol snapshot cannot reveal what was never logged, so a reader cannot distinguish a protocol written once from one converged upon, and no later audit can reconstruct it.

## Why it is open

The information is destroyed rather than merely unreported: once a decision log is not kept there is no artifact to demand, and the investigators themselves cannot supply it. Registration systems were designed for randomized trials, where the protocol precedes the data, and have no natural slot for a design developed against an existing dataset. Requiring a full multiverse imposes a cost proportional to the number of decisions, which for a longitudinal emulation is large, so the honest practice is also the expensive one.

## What has been tried

::: {.table-scroll}

| Work | What it contributes |
|---|---|
| [Hansford HJ, et al. Design and implementation of observational studies emulating a target trial. JAMA Netw Open 2026](https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2025.58262) | Sets out the design decisions and acknowledges that operational methods remain scenario dependent, which is the residual this problem names. |
| [Hansford HJ, Cashin AG, Jones MD, et al. Transparent reporting of observational studies emulating a target trial: the TARGET statement. JAMA 2025](https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2025.13350) | A 21-item checklist covering what the study did. It reports the final specification and is explicitly a reporting rather than a design instrument. |

:::

## Probable solution or research direction

Require prospective versioning, dated amendment and decision logs, and trusted timestamps, so the chronology is auditable rather than remembered; nothing added after the fact substitutes for this. Prespecify a primary emulation plus a principled design multiverse over the decisions known to move estimates, and keep the distinct estimands explicit when reporting the spread rather than pooling specifications that answer different questions. Hash the executable specification before outcome analysis, which makes prespecification checkable by a third party instead of taken on trust.

## Verification

::: {.verification-trail}
**Verdict.** Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.

**The source said.** "An emulation makes many defensible decisions: active comparator, washout period, time zero, grace period, how treatment episodes are constructed, censoring rules, follow-up length and outcome definition. Each has more than one reasonable answer, and the set of answers is the researcher's degrees of freedom. Design guidance now exists and states plainly that the operational methods remain scenario dependent, which means the guidance narrows the set without closing it. Registrations, where they exist, record only the specification that was finally run; they do not record the alternatives considered, the order in which decisions were made, or which decisions were revised after the data were inspected. A reader therefore cannot distinguish a protocol written once from one converged upon."

**What was wrong with it.** No auditor found the claim overstated. The proposed direction is sharpened: a protocol snapshot cannot reveal revisions that were never logged, so the requirement is prospective versioning with trusted timestamps rather than fuller reporting after the fact, and a specification sensitivity analysis has to keep the distinct estimands explicit rather than pooling them.

**Dissent.** literature dissented (supported): Nothing in the corpus records a decision log, a dated chronology of design choices, or the alternatives rejected during protocol development. Quality-assessment tools for observational comparative effectiveness studies, and comprehensive analyses of emulation practice in oncology, evaluate the specification that was published rather than the process that produced it. The entry's claim is about an artifact nobody keeps, which is consistent with its absence from a literature search: the evidence for it is the absence of any paper reporting one.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens
:   **open / overstated.** A final, unversioned protocol cannot reveal unlogged alternatives or their chronology, so an auditability gap can remain. However, this is primarily a governance and implementation problem rather than an unsolved inferential method. Prospective version control, amendment records, decision logs, and trusted timestamps can preserve the history directly. The categorical assertion that registrations retain only the final protocol is not established by technical reasoning, and an unlogged history is unavailable to an auditor but not necessarily destroyed. A full multiverse is neither required for provenance nor automatically interpretable: changing populations, comparators, strategies, or outcomes creates different estimands, so their estimates do not constitute an uncertainty distribution for one parameter. A hash establishes integrity only when paired with a trusted timestamp and does not prove that no alternative analysis existed. This is a roadmap and reporting-standard item rather than a high-severity statistical gap.

Grok 4.5, recency lens
:   **open / supported.** Registrations and TARGET record the final specification. Multiverse/specification-curve methods (e.g. Simonsohn et al.) and some observational-study preregistration guidance exist, but EU PAS / ClinicalTrials-style registries and TARGET do not require rejected alternatives, decision chronology, or outcome-blinded feasibility logs as first-class artifacts. Version-controlled hashed executable specs before outcome analysis are not standard. Cost of full multiverse remains unsolved. Open as stated.

glm
:   **open / supported.** The claim is coherent and proportionate. It states that registrations record only the final specification and not the alternatives considered or the chronology of decisions. The reason given—that registration systems were designed for randomized trials where the protocol precedes the data and have no natural slot for a design developed against an existing dataset—directly entails that the artifact required to settle the issue is not currently produced or demanded by these systems.

Decision path
:   `R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex`
